Subject: BlueArbor dedicated sizing: burst envelope + fallback routing

Hi Samira / Tim —

Thanks again for the call this week. As discussed, we want to lock a lightweight dedicated sizing plan so BlueArbor can commit to the proof-of-concept (PoC) and we can validate throughput & SLOs under a controlled burst scenario. Quick context and asks: 

- Goal: support a sustained 1.2M tokens/day workload with bursts up to ~12k tokens/sec for short windows (2–5 minutes).
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for standard chat flows (avg 120 tokens); fallback acceptable at 750ms.
- Immediate asks: 1) please share observed request shapes (prompt+response token distributions) and an expected peak concurrency profile, 2) confirm if any prompts are >1024 tokens, 3) identify procurement timing constraints.

I attached a short set of PoC questions to speed the sizing (initial_poc_questions.xlsx). Once we have your token profile, our infra team will model a slab proposal and recommended fallback routing (regional + model-variant fallbacks).

Next step: if OK, propose a 30-min follow-up Tues to review our draft slab proposal.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Ben / team —

Thanks — attaching the token profile. High level:
- Typical day: ~1.15M tokens/day; production peak windows during batch report generation and late-afternoon user sessions.
- Peak short bursts: we routinely see spikes that drive ~9k–14k tokens/sec for ~2–6 minutes when nightly jobs overlap with interactive sessions.
- Prompt mix: 72% short chat (input avg 45 tokens / output avg 90 tokens), 20% document-summary (input 400–1,200 tokens / output 250–1,000 tokens), 8% embeddings/rerank. We have a small tail of prompts up to ~1,500 tokens.
- Procurement: if sizing aligns, we can start PO in mid-June, pilot infra rollout the week after.

Attachment: bluearbor_poc_token_profile.csv

A couple of questions for your sizing math: what latency SLO should we target for the long prompt cases (document-summary) vs short chat? Also curious how Redwood models fallback behavior when a slab is saturated — is it regional spillover or model-variant throttling?

—Samira
Director of ML Products
BlueArbor Labs

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@bluearbor.ai>, Timothy O'Neill <tim@bluearbor.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 May 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueArbor dedicated sizing: burst envelope + fallback routing

On Fri, May 25, 2028 at 11:03 AM Samira Khan <samira@bluearbor.ai> wrote:
> High level: Typical day: ~1.15M tokens/day; peak short bursts ~9k–14k tokens/sec; prompt mix: 72% short chat, 20% doc-summary, tail up to ~1,500 tokens.

Thanks for the profile — I modeled three scenarios and called out where fallback routing is recommended. Summary below (numbers rounded):

Scenario A — PoC conservative (pilot slab):
- Provision: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized runtime), continuous batching enabled, KV prefix cache for repeated question patterns.
- Expected effective throughput: ~6k tokens/sec sustained per slab with 1.2–1.6x burst headroom via transient queueing.
- Tail behavior (1,000–1,500 token prompts): median latency ~520ms, p95 ~1,100ms.
- SLO fit: short chat (avg 120 tokens) p95 = 280–320ms — meets target. Long prompts exceed primary SLO; recommend separate routing.

Scenario B — Pilot with burst cushion (recommended for BlueArbor):
- Provision: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs + 25% reserved burst capacity in a hot spare pool.
- Effective throughput: ~11k tokens/sec elastic for 3–6 minute bursts.
- Tail behavior: long prompts handled on higher-memory nodes; p95 short chat = 260–310ms, doc-summary p95 = 680–820ms.
- SLO fit: meets 95th <350ms for short chat; long prompts fall within fallback SLO of <750ms when routed to high-memory nodes.

Scenario C — Full commit (for production SLA):
- Provision: 18 GPUs with two hot spares and cross-region failover.
- Throughput: sustained >18k tokens/sec; p95 short chat <240ms.

Fallback policy suggestions:
- Primary: route by request class (short-chat vs doc-summary). Short-chat pins to low-latency slab; doc-summary to high-memory slower slab.
- Secondary: regional spillover (if primary slab saturated, route to dedicated hot spare within region).
- Tertiary: model-variant throttle (quantized smaller model returns within degraded quality bounds) — used only when both slab + hot spare exhausted.

Operational notes and assumptions:
- Token/sec estimates assume continuous batching and KV cache hit rates ~25% for short-chat. If your cache hits are lower, p95 will move up ~10–15%.
- We recommend an initial telemetry window during the PoC to calibrate actual batching benefits and cold KV warm-up time; this often reduces required GPUs by 10–20% after warm-up.

Attached: redwood_slab_proposal_v1.pdf (detailed per-GPU math, queue modeling, cost delta table).

Action items:
- BlueArbor: confirm whether doc-summary prompts >1,024 tokens can be sharded or truncated (this materially affects slab choice).
- Redwood: schedule 30-min review next Tue to walk through the proposal and walk the procurement timeline.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Lead Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful and the scenario B numbers look like the right balance for our first month. Confirming two things:
1) We can restructure some doc-summary flows to shard across smaller chunks (down to ~600 tokens) which should nudge the p95 down for long prompts.
2) Can we lock a pilot start of 2028-06-08? Procurement is ready to process the PO if the final slab/cost table matches scenario B.

If that works, we accept the proposed follow-up Tues to review the PDF and finalize procurement steps.

Tim
